newsitem.title: INDIA: Landmine blast kills four party workers in India.
newsitem.headline: Landmine blast kills four party workers in India.

text.p: Four political activists were killed and five others wounded on Tuesday when leftwing militants set off a landmine in the southern Indian state of Andhra Pradesh, police said.

They said guerrillas from the Peoples War Group (PWG), a Maoist militant organisation, attacked the last vehicle in convoy carrying Congress party workers in Machareddy village, about 100 km (60 miles) north of the state capital Hyderabad.
The workers were heading to a party convention in a nearby village.
A Congress member of the federal parliament, M. Bagarreddy, and former state minister Shabbir Ali were travelling in another vehicle and escaped unhurt, police said.
The People's War Group (PWG) is part of the Naxalite movement, which was started in India in the 1960s by groups that split from the main communist party.
The PWG is considered the most violent of the Naxalite outfits and controls large forest tracts straddling the states of Andhra Pradesh, Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh and Orissa.
Naxalites, who reject the Indian government and want to set up a Maoist state of their own, killed 202 civilians and 45 policemen in Andhra Pradesh last year, according to state authorities.
